newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel volume still at index level.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel volume still at index level.

text.p: Options volume on Intel Corp continued to look like major index options volume as the stock fell in heavy trading after the company forecast slowing revenue and falling gross margins.
By 1445 CDT/1945 GMT, the semiconductor maker's stock was down 3-3/8 at 130-3/8 on more than 23.6 million shares, making it the most active stock on the Nasdaq stock market.
Intel options, traded on the American Stock Exchange, were by far the most active group. More than 100,000 contracts had changed hands by early afternoon.
"It's just wild trading out there," one trader said of the action in Intel options. He said there were probably 100 people at the Intel options trading station.
Trading was led by the 10,725 contracts that traded in the Intel April 130 calls. The option, which had open interest of roughly 9,975 contracts, fell four to 2-1/4.
Volatilitiy in that option rose to the lower 40 region from the upper 30's.
Other busy Intel options included the April 135 calls, which traded 9,935 contracts adn the April 130 put, with nearly 8,300.
Action spread to the long term options as well, where the January 1998 205 call traded more than 7,100 contracts. That option slipped 1/2 to 2-3/8 and had open interest of about 9,210 contracts.
The January 1998 170 call traded about 3,130 contracts.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said it did not appear that any of the activity in those two long term options on Intel was related as in a spree.
He added that in broader options trading, it appeared investors were beginning to roll some April positions out to farther months ahead of this week's expiration.

"As we get into this last week (of expiration) we should start to see some rolling activity," Schwartz said, citing in particular a couple trades at the Chicago Board Options Exchange in Sears, Roebuck and Co options.
The Sears April 50 calls traded more than 4,300 contracts and the October 45 calls traded 2,840.
"That looks like a roll," Schwartz said. "It looks like they bought back the April 50's and rolled out to the October 45's for a nice credit."
The April 50 calls were up 3/16 at 1/4 and the October 45 calls rose 1/2 to 5-3/8.
Elsewhere, Schwartz said some of the put activity in Coca-Cola Co could be put sellers as the stock rallied.
The April 55 put traded more than 5,300 contracts and the May 50, 55 and 60 puts each traded more than 1,300.
"Some of those May puts may be sales," Schwartz said. Coca-Cola shares rose 2-5/8 to 58-1/4, extending gains posted Monday after the company reported solid first quarter earnings.
